result:
The correct answer is $[\tfrac12,\infty)$, which Solutions 1 and 3 both give. Solution 2's $[\tfrac13,\infty)$ is inconsistent with the known sharpness of the exponent $\tfrac12$. I did not verify the convergence theorem at $p=\tfrac12$ or the sharpness construction from the literature; I'm relying on them as recalled.

Solution 2 claims $\sum\delta_j^{1/3}<\infty$, which would force convergence for $p\in[\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$. That contradicts the known divergence for every $p<\tfrac12$ (Drasin-type constructions). Its heuristic Hölder argument also doesn't establish the stated budgets.

Solutions 1 and 3 share the same structure: convergence for $p\ge\tfrac12$ from the Weitsman-type/Eremenko-type theorem, and sharpness by lifting a meromorphic example with $\sum\Delta_j^p=\infty$ into $\mathbb P^m$. Solution 3 is the more precise of the two. Its construction uses binomially weighted components, so that $\|F\|^2=(|f_0|^2+|f_1|^2)^m$ exactly, and its linear combinations are exactly $(f_1-c_jf_0)^m$. The general-position check via Vandermonde is correct. Solution 1 uses unweighted Veronese components, which still works up to bounded constants in $T_F$, but its argument is looser.

CHOICE: 3
